learn.rule: To revise, replace vague words with precise ones, add signal words that connect ideas, and add a specific detail.
learn.ruleEs: Para revisar, cambia las palabras vagas por palabras precisas, agrega palabras de señal que conecten las ideas y agrega un detalle específico.
learn.model: Weak: The storm was bad. Stronger: The hurricane flooded streets and knocked out power for three days.
learn.notice: The stronger sentence names what happened and gives details you can picture.

items.prompt: Choose the best revision of this vague sentence about volcanoes.

options.text: Volcanoes do really bad stuff.
Volcanic eruptions can destroy forests, bury towns in ash, and disrupt air travel.
Volcanoes are things that do bad stuff to places.
Volcanoes are bad.

items.why: The best revision swaps vague words like bad things for specific results you can picture.
items.whyEs: La mejor revisión cambia palabras vagas como bad things por resultados específicos que se pueden imaginar.

items.prompt: Check the changes that make this volcano draft stronger.

options.text: Replace 'stuff' with specific words such as lava, ash, and gas.
Add the word 'very' before every adjective.
Add a detail about why an eruption is dangerous, such as fast-moving lava or falling ash.
Begin every sentence with the word 'volcano.'
Replace 'cool' with a precise word such as 'powerful.'

items.why: Precise nouns, specific details, and exact adjectives strengthen a draft. Extra very words and repeated sentence starters do not.
items.whyEs: Los sustantivos precisos, los detalles específicos y los adjetivos exactos fortalecen un borrador. Las palabras very de más y los inicios repetidos no lo hacen.
items.text: Draft: Volcanoes are cool. They do bad stuff to towns. Lots of people have to leave.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word and the precise word.
parts: , the ash they leave behind eventually makes soil
items.model: Volcanoes can destroy towns. However, the ash they leave behind eventually makes soil fertile for farming.
items.why: However signals a contrast between destruction and benefit. Fertile is the exact word for soil that helps crops grow.
items.whyEs: However señala un contraste entre la destrucción y el beneficio. Fertile es la palabra exacta para un suelo que ayuda a crecer los cultivos.

items.prompt: Which revision fixes the repeated words in this draft?
items.text: The volcano erupted. The volcano shook the town. The volcano covered the town in ash.

options.text: The volcano erupted, shook the town, and covered it in ash.
The volcano erupted. The volcano shook the town. It covered the town in ash.
The volcano erupted, and the volcano shook the town, and the volcano covered the town.
The big volcano erupted. The big volcano shook the town. The big volcano covered the town in ash.

items.why: Combining the actions into one sentence removes the repeated words. The other choices still repeat volcano or town.
items.whyEs: Unir las acciones en una oración elimina las palabras repetidas. Las otras opciones todavía repiten volcano o town.

items.prompt: Put the revised volcano draft in order.
lines: Volcanoes are powerful forces that reshape the land.
First, hot magma rises through cracks in Earth's crust.
Then pressure builds until lava, ash, and gas burst out of the vent.
As a result, an eruption can bury nearby towns in ash and force families to leave.
However, old eruptions also leave soil rich enough to grow crops.
items.why: Signal words show the order: first, then, as a result. However adds a contrast, so it comes after the damage is described.
items.whyEs: Las palabras de señal muestran el orden: first, then, as a result. However agrega un contraste, así que va después de describir el daño.

write.prompt: Revise the draft. Replace vague words, add a signal word, and add at least one specific detail.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador. Cambia las palabras vagas, agrega una palabra de señal y agrega al menos un detalle específico.
write.text: Earthquakes are bad. They shake things. People get hurt.

label: My revision has at least 25 words
Mi revisión tiene al menos 25 palabras
I added a signal word such as because, however, or as a result
Agregué una palabra de señal como because, however o as a result
I used precise words such as plates, fault, buildings, or rubble
Usé palabras precisas como plates, fault, buildings o rubble
My last sentence ends with a period

write.model: Earthquakes can be extremely destructive. They happen when tectonic plates suddenly slip along a fault, which shakes the ground. As a result, buildings may collapse, and falling rubble can injure people.

familyTalk.en: Pick a weak sentence from a text message or note. Make it stronger with one exact word and one detail.
familyTalk.es: Elijan una oración débil de un mensaje o una nota. Háganla más fuerte con una palabra exacta y un detalle.

teacherTip.en: Circle vague words in the draft together, then let students brainstorm exact replacements in pairs.
teacherTip.es: Encierren juntos las palabras vagas del borrador y deja que las parejas piensen reemplazos exactos.

sets.title: Great Depression Revision Lab
sets.titleEs: Laboratorio de revisión: la Gran Depresión

learn.rule: To revise, replace vague words with precise ones, add signal words that connect ideas, and add a specific detail.
learn.ruleEs: Para revisar, cambia las palabras vagas por palabras precisas, agrega palabras de señal que conecten las ideas y agrega un detalle específico.
learn.model: Weak: Times were hard. Stronger: Banks closed, and families lost their savings overnight.
learn.notice: Exact facts replace the vague word hard.

items.prompt: Which revision replaces the vague word 'hard' with specific information?
items.text: The Great Depression was a hard time.

options.text: During the Great Depression, thousands of banks closed and about one in four American workers lost their jobs.
The Great Depression was a really hard time.
The Great Depression was a very sad and hard time for everyone.
The Great Depression was hard, hard, and hard.

items.why: Specific facts, such as bank closings and job losses, show how hard the time was. Extra adjectives do not add information.
items.whyEs: Los datos específicos, como el cierre de bancos y la pérdida de empleos, muestran qué tan difícil fue la época. Los adjetivos extra no agregan información.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that connects each pair of ideas.
parts: Many factories closed in the early 1930s.
, millions of workers lost their paychecks. Families found ways to cope.
, many planted gardens and shared food with neighbors.
items.model: Many factories closed in the early 1930s. As a result, millions of workers lost their paychecks. Families found ways to cope. For example, many planted gardens and shared food with neighbors.
items.why: As a result shows that closed factories caused lost paychecks. For example introduces specific ways families coped.
items.whyEs: As a result muestra que el cierre de las fábricas causó la pérdida de sueldos. For example presenta maneras específicas en que las familias se las arreglaron.

items.prompt: Check the revisions that make this draft stronger.

options.text: Replace 'hard time' with details such as bank closures and long lines for food.
Add 'very' and 'really' to the second sentence.
Replace 'lost jobs' with a clear number, such as 'about one in four workers.'
Write 'The Great Depression' at the beginning of every sentence.
Add a signal word like 'as a result' to show cause and effect.

items.why: Specific details, exact numbers, and signal words make the draft clearer. Extra intensifiers and repeated openings do not.
items.whyEs: Los detalles específicos, los números exactos y las palabras de señal hacen el borrador más claro. Los intensificadores de más y los inicios repetidos no lo hacen.
items.text: Draft: The Great Depression was a hard time. Many people lost jobs. It was bad everywhere.

items.prompt: Which revision removes the repeated words from this draft?
items.text: Families were poor. The poor families had little food. The poor families waited in long lines.

options.text: Families that were poor had little food, and the poor families waited in long lines.
The poor were poor and had little food.
Poor families had little food, so they waited in long lines.
Poor families were poor, and poor families waited.

items.why: The best revision joins the ideas and uses so to show the result. The other choices still repeat poor or lose a fact.
items.whyEs: La mejor revisión une las ideas y usa so para mostrar el resultado. Las otras opciones siguen repitiendo poor o pierden un dato.

items.prompt: Put the revised Great Depression paragraph in order.
lines: The Great Depression, which began after the 1929 stock market crash, caused widespread hardship.
First, thousands of banks closed, so many families lost their savings.
Next, about one in four workers lost their jobs.
As a result, long lines formed outside soup kitchens in many cities.
Even so, communities survived by sharing food and growing gardens.
items.why: The signal words first, next, and as a result show cause and effect in order. Even so closes with a contrast about resilience.
items.whyEs: Las palabras de señal first, next y as a result muestran causa y efecto en orden. Even so cierra con un contraste sobre la resistencia.

write.prompt: Revise the draft about the Gold Rush. Use precise facts, add a signal word, and make it longer.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador sobre la fiebre del oro. Usa datos precisos, agrega una palabra de señal y hazlo más largo.
write.text: The Gold Rush was big. Lots of people went to California. It changed things.
write.frame: The California Gold Rush, which began in ___

label: My revision has at least 25 words
Mi revisión tiene al menos 25 palabras
I added a signal word such as because, however, or as a result
Agregué una palabra de señal como because, however o as a result
I added a precise fact such as a year, a place, or a group of people
Agregué un dato preciso como un año, un lugar o un grupo de personas
My last sentence ends with a period
Mi última oración termina con punto

write.model: The California Gold Rush, which began in 1848, brought hundreds of thousands of people to the West. For example, San Francisco grew from a small village into a busy city within a few years. As a result, new towns, farms, and businesses changed the region.

familyTalk.en: Tell a family story and then retell it with exact names, places, and numbers. Notice how it improves.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten una historia familiar y luego vuelvan a contarla con nombres, lugares y números exactos. Noten cómo mejora.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to highlight vague phrases and replace each with a fact from their notes.
teacherTip.es: Pide que resalten las frases vagas y que reemplacen cada una con un dato de sus notas.

learn.rule: To revise, replace vague words with precise ones, add signal words that connect ideas, and add a specific detail.
learn.ruleEs: Para revisar, cambia las palabras vagas por palabras precisas, agrega palabras de señal que conecten las ideas y agrega un detalle específico.
learn.model: Weak: Dev is nice. Stronger: Dev waits after practice to help Sam learn the plays.
learn.notice: The stronger sentence shows what the character does instead of only saying nice.

items.prompt: Choose the revision that replaces 'good friend' with a precise trait and evidence.

options.text: Dev is a really good friend and a nice person.
Dev is a loyal friend who waits for Sam after practice, even when the bus is late.
Dev is a good friend because he is good.
Dev is a friend, and he is good, and he is a friend.

items.why: A precise word, loyal, plus a specific action makes the character real. The other choices repeat good without evidence.
items.whyEs: Una palabra precisa, loyal, y una acción específica hacen real al personaje. Las otras opciones repiten good sin evidencia.

items.prompt: Choose the more precise word for each blank.
parts: his notes with classmates who missed class, which shows he is
items.model: Dev shares his notes with classmates who missed class, which shows he is generous.
items.why: Shares and generous are exact words. Does, has, okay, and fine are vague and do not match the action.
items.whyEs: Shares y generous son palabras exactas. Does, has, okay y fine son vagas y no coinciden con la acción.

items.prompt: Check the changes that would strengthen the draft about Dev.

options.text: Replace 'nice things' with an example, such as lending his bike to a neighbor.
Add 'really' before 'good.'
Add 'for example' to introduce the evidence.
Delete all the details so the draft is shorter.
Replace 'Everyone likes him' with a specific result, such as 'his teammates trust him to be fair.'

items.why: Examples, signal words, and specific results strengthen the draft. Really and deleting details make it weaker.
items.whyEs: Los ejemplos, las palabras de señal y los resultados específicos fortalecen el borrador. Really y borrar los detalles lo debilitan.
items.text: Draft: Dev is a good friend. He does nice things. Everyone likes him.

items.prompt: Which revision adds the missing signal word between these two ideas?
items.text: Dev practiced the speech every night. He felt confident on stage.

options.text: Dev practiced the speech every night; however, he felt confident on stage.
Dev practiced the speech every night; for example, he felt confident on stage.
Dev practiced the speech every night; in contrast, he felt confident on stage.
Dev practiced the speech every night; as a result, he felt confident on stage.

items.why: Practice caused the confidence, so as a result shows the connection. However and in contrast signal an opposite, and for example would need an example.
items.whyEs: La práctica causó la confianza, así que as a result muestra la conexión. However e in contrast señalan algo opuesto, y for example necesitaría un ejemplo.

items.prompt: Put the revised paragraph about Dev in order.
lines: Dev is a loyal friend who puts other people first.
For example, he stays after practice to help Sam learn the plays.
He also shares his notes with classmates who missed class.
As a result, his teammates trust him and ask for his advice.
In short, Dev's actions show that loyalty means helping others, even when it costs him time.
items.why: The claim comes first, for example introduces the first proof, also adds more, and as a result shows the effect.
items.whyEs: La afirmación va primero, for example presenta la primera prueba, also agrega más y as a result muestra el efecto.

write.promptEs: Revisa este borrador de un cuento. Nombra el escenario, di qué pasó y muestra cómo se sintió el personaje.
write.text: The setting was scary. Things happened. The character felt bad.

write.model: The abandoned hallway was dark and silent, and the flickering light made every shadow look alive. Suddenly, footsteps echoed behind Rina, and her heart pounded against her ribs. As a result, she gripped her flashlight and forced herself to keep walking.

familyTalk.en: Describe a time you felt nervous without using the word nervous. Use what you saw, heard, and did.
familyTalk.es: Describan una vez en que se sintieron nerviosos sin usar la palabra nervous. Usen lo que vieron, oyeron e hicieron.

teacherTip.en: Model showing one feeling through action, then have students try it with a different emotion.
teacherTip.es: Muestra cómo expresar un sentimiento con una acción y luego pide que lo intenten con otra emoción.
